Regenerate with: python make_fixture.py --out fixtures/bikeshare.xlsx

evals.name: audit-before-committee
evals.prompt: I'm taking this financial model to our board on Thursday and I'm nervous about it. Can you go through fixtures/bikeshare.xlsx and tell me what they're going to find? I need to know which numbers won't survive being questioned.
evals.expected_output: Identifies the stock-times-flow double counting in the addressable-market formula and the subset-exceeds-total symptom; flags the unsourced assumptions (the AI-attributed item price, the cells marked 'Arbitrary assumption'); explains which assumptions carry Y3 net profit. Numbers reproducible from the workbook.
assertions: Identifies that the addressable-market formula multiplies daily active riders by campaign duration, counting the same people once per day (person-days rather than people)
Flags that the resulting addressable market exceeds the daily active rider base it derives from
Flags the average item price as unsourced, noting the model attributes it to ChatGPT analysis
Flags at least one assumption the model itself labels 'Arbitrary assumption'
Reports the parse was verified against the workbook's own cached values (48/48) before relying on any numbers
Distinguishes structural/formula defects from evidence-quality problems rather than presenting one undifferentiated list
Presents findings as flags for the modeller to confirm rather than asserting the model is simply wrong

evals.name: which-assumptions-matter
evals.prompt: Attached is our 3-year model (fixtures/bikeshare.xlsx). We have limited time for research before the board meeting. Which assumptions should we actually spend that time on, and why those? Target is Y3 net profit.
evals.expected_output: Runs sensitivity, reports that several assumptions tie on leverage because the merchandise chain is multiplicative, and breaks the tie using evidence quality — prioritising the arbitrary/AI-sourced high-leverage assumptions over the survey-sourced ones. Should NOT list every assumption or propose researching everything.
assertions: Performs an actual sensitivity computation (perturbing assumptions and recomputing the target) rather than reasoning qualitatively about which inputs seem important
Recognises that several assumptions in the merchandise revenue chain have identical leverage because that chain is multiplicative
Uses evidence quality (unsourced vs sourced) to break the leverage tie and set the research order
Recommends a short prioritised shortlist (roughly 3-8 assumptions) rather than all assumptions in the model
Explicitly deprioritises at least one high-leverage assumption because it is already well sourced (e.g. the rider survey figure)
Names the target cell or value it ranked against

evals.name: harden-and-deliver
evals.prompt: Please harden fixtures/bikeshare.xlsx so we can send it to a funder: I want every assumption to carry its source and confidence, the structural problems documented, and the whole thing back as a spreadsheet we can actually hand over. Also a one-page summary for the people who won't open Excel.
evals.expected_output: Produces a hardened .xlsx containing an Assumptions Ledger tab and Findings tab, with cell notes carrying provenance and input/formula colour coding, plus a standalone HTML summary. Original formulas preserved.
assertions: Produces a hardened .xlsx file as an output artifact
The hardened workbook contains an assumptions ledger worksheet listing assumptions with evidence/grade fields
The hardened workbook contains a findings worksheet documenting structural issues
Assumption cells in the hardened workbook carry provenance as cell comments/notes
All 3 original worksheets are preserved and original formulas still present (not replaced by static values)
Produces a standalone HTML summary file that opens without external dependencies
The delivered spreadsheet is the source workbook augmented, not a newly invented workbook
